timeline.summary: The First Light lander touches down on the Shackleton Crater rim; crew and player are introduced.
Habitat inflated, solar array connected, compressed oxygen valve opened, CDRA scrubbers powered; cabin balanced at 21% O2 and 101.3 kPa.
Primary compressed oxygen tank valve fractures; less than 48 hours of breathable air remain; the player must demand an emergency resupply from Earth.
The emergency cargo lander arrives after a 2-sol transit and Amir swaps the oxygen tanks; oxygen returns to 100%.
A mountain ridge will shadow the base for 48 consecutive hours; no solar power; outside temperature falls to -180 C.
During the dark, Battery Bank 2 cooling lines freeze and cabin temperature falls (18, 12, 6 C) until heating is rerouted and stabilizes at 21 C.
DONKI alert: an X-class flare from sunspot 4109 sends a CME along the Earth-Moon line; the proton shockwave arrives in 90 minutes.
The radiation storm hits (exterior 140 mSv/h); the crew survives in the storm vault behind regolith and water-tank shielding.
Earth rations are down to the last week; the player starts water-ice extraction in the crater.
Hydroponic lettuce and radishes planted in greenhouse trays; the first sprouts grow.
Moonquake cuts power to life support, dust covers the solar arrays, and cabin oxygen leaks while Captain Leo is stuck outside at a jammed valve.
The player restores power and repressurizes the airlock; Leo is pulled inside alive.
Mission debrief, commendation and the First Light diploma.
NASA transmits a new expedition target: Mars, 225 million km away.

facts.text: The landing site is about 384,000 km from Earth.
No human can breathe on the Moon without life support.
If power dies the heaters die; if the air tanks run dry the crew dies.
Habitat oxygen comes from high-pressure tanks delivered with the lander and is not infinite.
Without powered CDRA scrubbers, carbon dioxide poisons the crew within hours.
The balanced cabin atmosphere is 21% O2 at 101.3 kPa.
After the valve fracture, less than 48 hours of breathable air remain.
Panic consumes more oxygen.
The emergency resupply transit takes 2 sols.
A resupply delay of half a day would have been fatal.
A mountain ridge will shadow the base for 48 consecutive hours.
Solar panels produce nothing in shadow and outside temperature falls to -180 C.
Without heaters the habitat interior drops below freezing in about two hours.
Excess solar power must be stored in batteries before the shadow arrives.
Frozen cooling lines stop a battery bank from releasing power.
Cabin temperature fell from 18 to 12 to 6 C before the heaters were rerouted.
Rerouted heating loops stabilize the cabin at 21 C.
NASA DONKI reports an X-class flare from sunspot 4109.
A CME along the Earth-Moon line brings a proton radiation shockwave in 90 minutes.
Standard habitat walls are thin aluminum and Kevlar and do not stop the storm.
Protection needs regolith piled over the roof and an underground bunker surrounded by water tanks.
Exterior radiation spiked to 140 mSv/h; anyone outside would suffer fatal organ failure in 15 minutes.
Inside the bunker, water tanks and regolith absorb the radiation and the dosimeter reads safe.
Packaged rations from Earth are down to their last week.
Ancient water ice lies deep inside Shackleton's shadow and can be extracted with a thermal drill.
The water extractor yields +10 L/h of purified water.
Hydroponic plants use recycled wastewater, absorb CO2, and give food and oxygen.
A moonquake cut main power to life support, dust covered the solar arrays, and cabin pressure fell below 70 kPa.
Captain Leo is outside; the emergency valve is jammed by dust and his oxygen is running out.
Leo has about 60 seconds before he suffocates.
Power is restored by four player steps; the airlock repressurizes and Leo survives.
The next target is Mars, 225 million km away.

review_flags.issue: The source is a single linear story from the player's console. It has no separate starting points.
review_flags.evidence: One campaign (Prologue to Epilogue); the TOC lists a Campaign Structure section but it is empty.
review_flags.suggested_action: The story team defines 3 starting points with different start sols and scenes. The four crew perspectives in this JSON are mechanical drafts (scenes where each character speaks) and must be authored or replaced.

review_flags.issue: The TOC lists 'Production Data Schema (JSON)' and a Campaign Structure and Arc section, but neither exists in the file.
review_flags.suggested_action: Send them if they exist elsewhere; this JSON follows the project's own story-bible schema instead.

review_flags.issue: The story gives durations (2 sols transit, 48 h shadow, last week of rations) but no sol numbers or mission length.
review_flags.evidence: Failure screen example says Sol 34; the plan says about 10-15 sols.
review_flags.suggested_action: Team picks the real mission length and event sols; all sols here are provisional (mission 15 sols).

review_flags.issue: 'Sol' is a Mars day. The story uses it for the Moon.
review_flags.suggested_action: Either define 'sol' in-game as a 24 h game day (explain it to kids) or use 'day'.

review_flags.issue: Radiation numbers are internally inconsistent and likely unrealistic: 'fatal above 80 mSv/h', exterior 140 mSv/h, 'fatal organ failure in 15 minutes'. At 140 mSv/h, 15 minutes is about 35 mSv.
review_flags.evidence: General knowledge (NOT verified against a NASA source here): acute radiation sickness generally needs doses of hundreds of mSv up to about 1 Sv received quickly. The project's own unverified seed fact puts ISS exposure at about 0.2-0.5 mSv per day.
review_flags.suggested_action: Ask the mentor. Either label these as fictional game values, or rework into a cumulative-dose mechanic with limits from a cited NASA source.

review_flags.issue: Chapter 3 is a scripted X-class flare from 'sunspot 4109'. The project plan wants DONKI-driven real events; DONKI samples saved in this project use 5-digit active region numbers (for example 14513).
review_flags.suggested_action: Decide: keep a scripted story beat but label it fictional, or drive the beat from real DONKI statistics (/events/profile) and drop the invented sunspot number.

review_flags.issue: Three different oxygen variables and thresholds: stored_o2 tank, cabin O2 % (fatal at or below 5%), and the failure rule 'oxygen == 0'. Pressure also has two thresholds (alert below 70 kPa, failure at or below 10).
review_flags.suggested_action: Define exactly which variables exist and which one the evaluator reads. Align the failure screen triggers.

review_flags.issue: The story uses far more than the 3 core resources (also temperature, pressure, CO2, water, food).
review_flags.suggested_action: Map each to power / oxygen / shielding (for example temperature to power, pressure to oxygen) or consciously extend scope. Kids are best served by 2-3 resources.

review_flags.issue: After the fracture there are 'less than 48 hours' of air, and the resupply takes 2 sols. If a sol is 24 h, air runs out at about the moment the rocket lands, so conservation is mandatory.
review_flags.suggested_action: If this is intended, state the oxygen drain rule so the evaluator can score conservation choices.

review_flags.issue: Most decisions have no stated cost, which breaks the design rule that every choice has a trade-off. Rule 5 of the story validator will fail until costs and deltas exist.
review_flags.evidence: cost_status is 'missing' for most decisions in this file.
review_flags.suggested_action: Game devs and AI side define deltas and delayed effects per decision (see context/game-design.md).

review_flags.issue: The epilogue hardcodes 'Survival Rate: 100%, Life-Support Uptime: 98.4%' and the failure screen hardcodes 'Sol 34'.
review_flags.suggested_action: Use evaluator output and the real sol of failure; keep these as placeholders in the story.

review_flags.issue: Dr. Nia Okafor has no lines in Chapter 5 (the convergence scene), so her derived perspective crew_nia does not reach the convergence event and breaks validator rule 3.
review_flags.suggested_action: Give Nia a presence in the catastrophe (for example at her science terminal), or drop her from the 3 chosen starting points.

review_flags.issue: Leo is 'Mission Commander' while the player is addressed as 'Commander'.
review_flags.suggested_action: Rename one (for example the player is 'Junior Commander' or 'Operator').

open_questions: Names, start sols and unique scenes of the 3 Kaleidoscope starting points
Real mission length and event sols

Which oxygen/pressure variables the game really tracks
Whether radiation values stay fictional or follow a cited NASA source
